instructors.name: Randy Hensley
instructors.summary: Randy Hensley has been involved with defensive driver training since 1987.
instructors.bio: After a brief career in oilfield sales, Randy returned to San Angelo to help his father, David L. Hensley, teach defensive driving. His career has stayed in education, and his instructive skills were critical in the development of the online course.

instructors.name: Gary Hensley
instructors.summary: Gary Hensley has continuously taught classroom defensive driving since 1992.
instructors.bio: The school’s August 2026 instructor biography reports that Gary had presented the defensive driving course more than 2,000 times. When Texas Defensive Driving School created its online course, Gary's classroom experience helped shape the online course curriculum.

faqs.question: Do I need court permission before taking defensive driving for a ticket?
faqs.answer: Yes. Contact the court named on your citation before enrolling for ticket dismissal. The court, not TexDDS, decides eligibility, court costs, deadlines, and which completion documents it will accept.

faqs.question: How long is the Texas defensive driving course?
faqs.answer: The licensed Texas driving safety course is six hours. TexDDS offers its ticket-dismissal course online, subject to court approval for dismissal.

faqs.question: How much does the TexDDS online defensive driving course cost?
faqs.answer: The TexDDS online defensive driving course is $25 flat. There is no separate $3 materials or administration fee and no electronic delivery fee. Driver-record and insurance-course options are priced separately.

faqs.question: Can I take the course on a phone, and is there a final exam?
faqs.answer: TexDDS describes the online course as video-based and mobile-friendly for phones, tablets, and desktop computers. The course does not have a final exam.

faqs.question: What happens after I finish the course?
faqs.answer: Follow the TexDDS completion steps, then submit the certificate and any other required documents exactly as your court or insurer directs. TexDDS does not add an electronic delivery fee; the receiving court or insurer controls its own deadline and submission format.

faqs.question: Do I need a Type 3A Texas driver record?
faqs.answer: Many courts require one, but follow the instructions from the court named on your citation. Texas DPS identifies Type 3A as the driver-record type used for defensive driving.

faqs.question: What is included in the course and driver-record bundle?
faqs.answer: The $44.95 bundle combines the $25 defensive driving course with Type 3A driver-record ordering support. The record option is $5 less in the bundle than the $24.95 standalone record service.

faqs.question: Can I take defensive driving for an insurance discount?
faqs.answer: TexDDS offers a separate six-hour, $15 insurance-discount course. Ask your insurer whether it qualifies before enrolling. That option is not a ticket-dismissal course unless a court has separately approved your case and directed you to an eligible course.

faqs.question: Is Texas Defensive Driving School licensed by Texas?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation lists Texas Defensive Driving School as a current Driving Safety Provider under license CP411. Directory inclusion verifies license status and is not a TDLR endorsement.

faqs.question: Is TexDDS online statewide, and are classroom courses available?
faqs.answer: The online course serves eligible drivers across Texas. TexDDS also offers scheduled or appointment-based in-person classes at its San Angelo classroom; call ahead for the next available date.
